questions.question: The SI unit of Potential difference is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**volt.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The SI unit of Potential difference is volt.**

** Potential Difference (Voltage):**

 
• The energy required to transfer the unit of charge point from one point to another point is known as a Potential Difference (Voltage).
 
• Mathematically, Potential Difference (Voltage) can be expressed as,
 
 
• **Voltage (V) = W/Q.**
 
• Where W is the work done in Joule,
 
• and Q is charge in Coulomb.
 
 
 
• **Hence, the SI unit for Potential Difference (Voltage) will be J/C also known as Volt.​**

questions.question: Which of the following has the same dimension as pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stress.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stress is developed in a body** when it is **subjected to a deforming force**.
 
• An opposite and equal force develops in response to the force applied.
 
• The restoring force per unit area of a body is called **stress**. The restoring force is equal to and the opposite of the deforming force applied to the body. It can also be defined as the deforming force per unit area of the body.
 
• So it has the same dimensions as that of pressure **(force/area). **
 
• **Dimension of Pressure and Stress: **M L⁻¹ T⁻²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strain**__** **

 __
 
• It is the **result of stress** experienced by the body.
 
• It may be observed in the **form of physical deformation** undergone by the body.
 
• It can be measured as the ratio of change in dimension to the original dimension.
 
• So it is **unitless**.
 
 
 
• **Work**__
 __
 
• It is a measure of energy expended to move an object over a certain distance.
 
• It is expressed as the **product of the force**(required to move the object) **and the displacement.**
 
• So its dimensions are **ML²T⁻²**.
 
 
 
• **Force**__** **
 
 
• In physics, a force is an influence that can change the motion of an object. 
 
• It is an external agent that results in a change in the state(rest or motion) of an object.
 
• It is expressed as the **product of mass**(of the object under change of state) **and acceleration** (of the object during the change).
 
• So its dimensions are **MLT⁻².**

questions.question: The dimension equivalent to joule is:
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Work done: The dot product of force and displacement is called work done.

 
 
• The SI unit of work is the **joule (J).**
 
 

Work done (W) = F.s cos θ 

Where F is force, s is displacement and θ is the angle between F and s.

Dimensional formula of work (W) = [ML2T-2]

 
• Energy: The capacity to do work is called energy.

 
 
• The SI unit of energy is the **joule (J)**.
 
 

Energy (E) = Work done (W)

Dimensional formula of Energy (E) = dimensional formula of work done (W) = [ML2T-2]

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• The **dimensional equivalent to joule is** [ML2T-2]. So option 3 is correct.

questions.question: The distance covered by a particle in time 't' is given by s = at + bt² where 'a' and 'b' are two constants. The dimensional formula of 'b' is:
questions.solution:
__Concept__:

Principle of homogeneity of dimensions:

__
 
• According to this principle, a physical equation will be dimensionally correct if the dimensions of all the terms occurring on both sides of the equation are the same.
 
• This principle is based on the fact that only the physical quantities of the same kind can be added, subtracted, or compared.
 
• Thus, velocity can be added to velocity but not to force.

Explanation:__

__**Given: **__

s = at + bt², From the dimensional homogeneity principle, the equation's left-hand side is dimensionally equal to the right-hand side. So, the dimensions of (s), (at), and (bt²) are the same.

The dimension formula of distance (s) = [L]

**For the first term:**

∴ [L] = [a] [T]

⇒ [ a ] =([L])/([T])=[LT⁻¹]

**For the second term:**

⇒ [L] = [b] [T²]

⇒ [b ] =([L])/([T²])=[LT⁻²]

The dimensional formula of 'b' is **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻²]**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dimensionless entity?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The powers to which fundamental quantities must be raised in order to express the given physical quantity are called its dimensions.
 
• A quantity without dimension will usually be a ratio of two quantities with similar dimensions and hence, will cancel out. Thus, they will have no units.

EXPLANATION__: 

 
• **Velocity:** It is defined as the **rate of change of displacement **i.e.

Rightarrow Velocity = (Displacemnt)/(Time)=([L])/([T])=[LT⁻¹]

∴ Velocity is not the dimensionless quantity.

 
• Angle: It is defined as the ratio of the length of arc to the radius, i.e.,

​Angle ( theta ) = frac{{length of arc ( l )}}{{radius ( r )}}

 Rightarrow theta = frac{{[ {{M⁰}L{T⁰}} ]}}{{[ {{M⁰}L{T⁰}} ]}} = 1

∴ An angle is a dimensionless quantity

 
• Mass is a not dimensionless quantity. as the** dimension of mass **is **[M]**.
 
• The **area **is a not dimensionless quantity. as the dimension of the area is [L²].

questions.question: The dimensional formula of speed
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Measurement of any physical quantity involves comparison with a certain basic, arbitrarily chosen, internationally accepted reference standard called unit, and a Dimension is a mathematical tool used for studying the nature of physical quantities. 
 
• The basic concept of dimensions is that we can add or subtract only those quantities which have the same dimensions.
 
• And the dimensional formula is defined as the expression of the physical quantity in terms of mass, length, and time.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• **Speed **is defined as the **rate of change of distance** i.e.,

Rightarrow Speed (v) = (Distance (d))/(time (t))

As we know, the dimension formula of distance (d) = [L]

The dimension formula of time (t) = [t]

∴ The dimension formula of speed is 

Rightarrow v =([L])/([T])=[M⁰LT⁻¹]

questions.question: Siemens is the unit of ______.
questions.solution:
__Explanation__:

Radiant intensity:

 
• It is defined as the amount of radiation emitted by a surface in a given direction per unit solid angle per unit area of that surface normal to the mean direction in space.
 
• Its unit is a watt per steradian

​Electric conductance:

 
• For a given voltage difference, electric conductance measures how easily electricity conducts through the electrical components 
 
• **Its unit is Siemens.**

Permeability:

 
• It is the ability of the object that allows the magnetic flux to pass through it when the object is placed in a magnetic field.
 
• Its unit is Henry/meter or Newton/ampere square.

Permittivity:

 
• It is defined as the ratio of electric displacement to the electric field intensity.
 
• Its unit is Farad/meter.

Thus, option (1) is the correct answer.
